name: Cross-instance Messaging
summary: Processes on different Atlas instances exchange messages through a durable, addressed and authorized channel: a published, versioned process interface (ADR-0373), a qualified address and envelope (ADR-0369), delivery as a Worker job acknowledged once on the receiver's disk (ADR-0372), and a participant that names an interface rather than a node (ADR-0371, Proposed).
next_action: CIM0: the owner describes the planned instances (how many, which roles, whether one is central, whether any crosses an organisation) so the open questions of ADR-0369 and ADR-0373 can be answered; then CIM1, ADR-0372's first cut: a peer Worker Type naming a configured peer, the full envelope, delivery to waiting subscriptions and the buffer only.

slices.title: Topology, trust and open questions
slices.note: Programme registered at the owner's request on 2026-11-05 with several instances planned; their description is still to come. Answer ADR-0369's open question (is a peer always an Atlas, do peers cross organisations) and ADR-0373's (per-publisher grant or a central catalogue); threat model for peer credentials on top of ADR-0129 and ADR-0410; decide ADR-0371 (Proposed).

slices.title: First cut: deliver to a configured peer
slices.note: ADR-0372 'The first cut': a reserved peer Worker Type whose Worker is a configured peer (base URL and vault credential reference, an ADR-0129 target); the whole ADR-0369 envelope including messageId and conversationId; the send step completes only when the receiver has the envelope past fsync; the receiver delivers to waiting subscriptions and the ADR-0370 buffer, never to a message start; a scoped token that may deliver to this node and nothing else; recovery tests on both sides.

slices.title: Published process interface
slices.note: ADR-0373: a versioned descriptor derived from a deployed definition — entry points, payloads, returns, terminal outcomes, commitments — published on purpose, with read and send grants kept apart; HTTP, MCP and Console.

slices.title: Qualified entry points and start by message
slices.note: ADR-0369's full address (node, interface, contract version, entry point): a peer may start an instance only through a published entry point, authorized by that interface's send grant; a peer message never enters messageStarts unqualified.

slices.title: A participant names an interface
slices.note: ADR-0371 once accepted: atlas:interfaceRef and atlas:entryPoint in the model, the node resolved per server, checked at deploy; the Worker stops being the address.

slices.title: Replies, errors and commitments across instances
slices.note: The returns an interface promises — reply messages, BPMN errors, escalations — travel back on the conversationId; a commitment's deadline is something a consumer models as a boundary timer, because there is no transaction across two logs.

slices.title: Operations across instances
slices.note: What is in flight between nodes and where it waits, in the Console, MCP and /metrics; cross-instance flows in the estate view of ADR-0402; incidents that name the peer.

slices.title: Intermittent peers (edge profile)
slices.note: With IOT7 of the Device Automation programme: a node that is unreachable for hours; sends that park visibly and resume; message lifetimes that outlast an outage; what an edge node may decide alone.
